contexts.text: They who have been spiritual men, with whom the Natural has been rightly subordinated, appear becomingly with long hair. From the hair in the other life it may be Known of what quality they are as to the Natural. The reason Spirits appear with hair, is that in the other life Spirits appear exactly like men on earth. Hence, too, it is, that the Angels seen in the Word are described also as to their hair. Illustrated.
Not to let down the hair () = not to reject what is natural, but to accommodate it so that it may agree; thus to subordinate it.

Therefore the Angels have hair, becomingly and ordinately arranged; their hair represents their natural life, and its correspondence with their spiritual life. That hair = the things which are of the natural life. References. To clip the hair = to accommodate natural things so that they may be becoming, and thus ornamental.

Such (worldly women) in the other life appear with long and spread hair over the face, which they comb... for to comb the hair = to accommodate natural things so that they may appear becoming. SE 1228.
Spirits may know from the hair; its colour, length, diffusion; of what quality they had been as to their natural life in the world. SE 1229.

As the Nazarites represented the Lord as to the Word in its ultimates... it was a statute for them, that they should make the hair grow, and shave off none of it. Moreover Nazarite, in the Hebrew language, means the hair.
They who have loved the sense of the letter of the Word, appear there in becoming hair. Compare TCR 223:2.
Such... appear naked, with the hair spread about, not flowing upon the back, but cut around, and covering the head like a mop.
It is from this correspondence that the Angels appear beautifully with long hair.
The ultimate sense of the Word, which is the sense of the letter, and to which also the hair corresponds.
